body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: a6ff9d2f991c3d6510b55b10cb14a8c00e243068 -->

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Test/docs PR (Refs #4154, P2). No planner code, no existing test or golden change: the diff is 18 new/added lines-only files, all under `crates/motion/tests/`, `crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start/` and `docs/decisions/`. Measurements run on the head locally (see "Where they ran").

What looks good
- The measures are genuinely test-only: the 7 files of `crates/motion/tests/common/law_measure/` read nothing from the planner — they never call a planner function; they take a finished `Toolpath`, a stock outline, a top, a part, holes, a reach and a limit, and they reuse the verifier's own crossing law and the rim meter. Nothing under `crates/motion/src/`, `crates/app/src/`, `crates/sim/`, `crates/post/` is touched (`git diff --stat origin/side/path-kernel pr-4167-review`).
- The readings are pinned as they are today, with the "Breaks today" column matching the table rows row for row (checked against each `pin(...)` call in the test files); every row of the PR body's table matches the pinned table in the tests byte for byte.
- The fig8 cases join the existing suite by `#[path]` (no new test binary, no new crate edge, no `Cargo.toml` change), and the one new top-level binary (`crates/motion/tests/kernel_laws.rs`) carries a reason in the body.
- The fig8 heavy tests carry a light twin by the light-lane rule (`<full test>_light` + `light lane:` ignore reason), except 2D Contour, which has one case and so has no reduced set — the body says so.
- The decision record `docs/decisions/4154-law-measures.md` matches the tree: the law marks (link/L4/L5/L6 with the tolerance and the named-slot list), the "Dropped" list, and the cost-to-change all line up with the code.

Where they ran: locally on this host (not the runner — the dispatcher instructed a local review), in `.claude/worktrees/cc-pr4167-review` on branch `pr-4167-review` off `a6ff9d2f9` (trial merge with `origin/side/path-kernel`: already up to date, no conflicts).

- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test kernel_laws`: **28 passed, 0 failed** (17.3 s) — includes the 12 law_measure unit tests on hand-made toolpaths.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test offset_pass_start fig8` (default lane): **3 passed, 0 failed** (37.9 s): `kernel_laws_fig8::fig8_pocket_2d_readings_of_the_old_planner` plus the two pre-existing fig8 tests; the heavy fig8 tests and the three light twins are correctly `#[ignore]`d (16 ignored).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: **clean** (2m 09s).
- `cargo xtask gate light --base origin/side/path-kernel`: **7 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (1.9 min, wall 1.9 min)** — includes the three new twins `app light: offset_pass_start` (fig8_adaptive_2d / fig8_offset_2d / fig8_pocket_3d light twins), ok in 50 s.
- Quick gate dry-run against `origin/side/path-kernel`: 161 steps, matching the body. Not run in full — the touched suites above are the applicable subset (this is a P2 test PR).
- Example catalog suites: not run (no post or toolpath change). Heavy step: not run — P2.

Requested before merge: nothing blocking.

Notes (non-blocking):
- The PR body's claim "It changes no ... existing test" is slightly imprecise: `crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start.rs` and `crates/motion/tests/common/mod.rs` are modified to declare the new modules. No existing test or assertion changes; the body reads as though no test file is touched. Consider a one-line clarification.
- `fixture.rs`, `laws_*.rs` and `measure_units.rs` do not carry the one-line provenance comment that `law_measure/mod.rs`, `kernel_laws.rs` and `kernel_laws_fig8.rs` do. A single shared line at the top of `kernel_laws.rs` probably covers them, but the AGENTS.md rule asks each module for one.
- The body ends with `Refs #4154` rather than `Fixes #4154`. The issue's done-means is met by this head, so if it is intended to close the issue, `Fixes #4154` would be the honest line; if the kernel switch (a later PR) is meant to close it, `Refs` is right.
- `lazy` pin-message format: the `pin` helper prints `places` as `Debug`; fine for a failure message.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
